# Pioneer SCHISM-AED Modelling Guide {.unnumbered}

Welcome to the **Pioneer SCHISM-AED Modelling Guide** — a practical walkthrough
of the Pioneer estuary coupled hydrodynamic–biogeochemical model and its
analytics, intended to let a new user step through the model setup, run it, and
analyse its outputs.

::: {.callout-note}
This guide is in draft and under active development. Structure and content are
subject to change.
:::

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="58%"}
The model resolves the tidal circulation of the Pioneer estuary on an
unstructured mesh, coupled to a full biogeochemical state. The animation
alongside shows the depth-averaged current speed over a spring–neap window — the
flood and ebb pulses that drive exchange between the river, the estuary and the
coastal ocean, and which the conservation tests in this guide must account for.

From this physical circulation the coupled model carries salinity, temperature,
dissolved oxygen, nutrients and tracers — the basis for the analysis, animation
and nutrient-budget workflows documented here.
:::

## What this covers {.unnumbered}

The Pioneer model couples **SCHISM** (Semi-implicit Cross-scale Hydroscience
Integrated System Model) — an unstructured-grid 3D hydrodynamic model — with
**AED** (Aquatic EcoDynamics), a biogeochemistry library that adds tracer
chemistry, dissolved oxygen, nutrient cycling and sediment processes. The
combined `pschism_AED` executable solves physics and biogeochemistry in one
MPI run.

This guide is organised into five parts:

1. **Introduction** — what the model is, key references, the Pioneer application,
   and how this repository is laid out.
2. **Model Setup** — every input file: mesh, vertical grid, boundary/tidal
   forcing, atmospheric and river forcing, AED configuration, and initial
   conditions.
3. **Model Analysis** — the output file structure, how to read the NetCDF
   outputs, and the animation toolkit.
4. **Nutrient Budget** — the control-volume mass-balance framework and the
   Pioneer-mouth flux investigation built on it.
5. **Running the Model** — building from source, running a simulation,
   combining outputs, and the record of run scenarios.

## How to use this guide {.unnumbered}

The parts are written to be read in order by a new user, but each chapter is
self-contained enough to use as a reference. Code, file names, and paths are
shown in `monospace`; chapters link to the actual scripts and configuration in
the repository wherever possible.

## Building this document {.unnumbered}

This guide is prepared in [Quarto](https://quarto.org). From `docs/quarto/`:

```bash
quarto preview      # live dev server
quarto render       # full build → _output/
```
